title: Claim payouts require a quorum of three experts while the Technical Committee has one active member
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.6 sets the decision rule: "[d]ecisions related to claim payouts require a quorum of three (3) experts from the Resilience Technical Committee with a simple majority (>50%)." The Active Data listing the Committee's membership (A.2.9.1.1.1.2.3.0.6.1) names one member.

The quorum rule is sound in itself — three experts with a majority prevents a single assessor's judgment from deciding discretionary payouts, which matters given that the recommendation is unappealable. But it is stated as a hard requirement, not a target, and the five-working-day recommendation window in A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.5 runs regardless of whether three experts exist to convene.

The result is a process that is formally blocked at its central step. A beneficiary can be onboarded, obtain pre-approved counsel, and file a compliant Payout Claim, and there is still no quorate body to assess it.

The underlying cause is traceable to the eligibility bar at A.2.9.1.1.1.2.2.1–.2.2.5, which requires dual legal/insurance and crypto credentials plus a bar on any outside business activity. The membership requirements and the quorum requirement were written to serve the same goal — independent expert judgment — and in combination they prevent it. This is the kind of coupling that only surfaces when the roster is read against the process rules.
description: A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.6 demands three experts and a simple majority; the Active Data roster lists a single member, so the quorum rule cannot currently be satisfied by the body that must satisfy it.
